title: Activating a licensed framework moves it from Available to Active and exposes View Compliance Map
preconditions: Logged in as a user with compliance.create
Target framework is licensed for the org but not yet added to the project
steps: Navigate to /grc-framework
Locate the framework tile in the 'Available Frameworks' section and click 'Activate'
Observe the tile move and a success toast
Click 'View Compliance Map' on the now-active tile
expectedResult: The framework tile moves to 'Active Frameworks' immediately (optimistic UI update), a success toast reads '<name> is now active.', and clicking 'View Compliance Map' navigates to /grc-framework/:id/compliance-map showing that framework's control list.

title: Deactivating an active framework shows an impact summary and moves it back to Available on confirm
preconditions: A framework with a non-zero controlCount is currently active
steps: On /grc-framework, click 'Deactivate' on an active framework tile
Read the confirmation modal's Impact Summary
Click 'Deactivate' to confirm
expectedResult: The modal shows '<N> controls will no longer be tracked' and warns the compliance map/coverage will stop updating. After confirming, the tile moves to 'Available Frameworks', a success toast appears, and the framework's compliance map data is no longer surfaced as active for this project.

title: Clicking Activate on an unlicensed framework shows the Upgrade Required modal and never calls the activation API
preconditions: Target framework has isLicensed:false for this org
steps: On /grc-framework, locate an unlicensed framework tile (shows 'Upgrade Required' button)
Click the button
Observe network activity during the click
expectedResult: An 'Upgrade Required' modal opens explaining the framework isn't licensed and to contact an administrator. No POST to /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/frameworks fires — the gate is enforced client-side before any network call, and would also be rejected server-side (403 LICENSING_REQUIRED) if bypassed.

title: Opening a control from the domain accordion shows the 7-dimension resource-metrics grid and resource table in the drawer
preconditions: Framework is active with at least one control that has evidence, a policy, a vendor mapping and a linked risk
steps: Navigate to /grc-framework/:id/compliance-map
Expand a domain accordion section
Click a control row that shows non-zero 'direct' and 'automated' counts
expectedResult: The Control Detail drawer opens showing: Evidence/Policy/Certs/Cloud/Integration/Vendor/Risk score tiles, a Resources table listing each attached item with type/source/last-updated, and a Related Risks section listing linked risks with severity and status badges.

title: Exporting with active filters produces a CSV containing only the filtered controls, in two sections
preconditions: Compliance map is loaded with more controls than match a chosen filter
steps: Set statusFilter to 'gap' and search for a keyword that matches a handful of controls
Click 'Export Filtered CSV'
Open the downloaded file
expectedResult: Button label reads 'Export Filtered CSV' (vs 'Export CSV' with no filters). The downloaded file is named '<framework>-compliance-map-<date>.csv', opens correctly in Excel (UTF-8 BOM preserved, no mojibake on the '·' domain separator), and contains a Control Summary section followed by a blank line and a Resource Detail section — both restricted to only the controls currently matching the active filters.

title: Refresh on the frameworks catalog page bypasses the compliance-summary cache and shows updated coverage
description: handleRefresh calls complianceService.refreshProjectSummary(projectId) before reloading — this forces aggregationService.refreshProjectSummary to recompute and re-cache ClientComplianceSummary, bypassing its 1-hour staleness threshold.
preconditions: Some evidence was just approved, changing a control's coverageScore, but the project's ClientComplianceSummary cache is still within its 1-hour freshness window
steps: Navigate to /grc-framework and note an active framework's displayed coverage %
Approve evidence elsewhere that changes that framework's underlying coverage
Return to /grc-framework and click 'Refresh'
expectedResult: The Refresh button shows a loading state ('Refreshing'), then the framework tile's coverage % and status badge update to reflect the just-approved evidence — not the stale cached value that a plain page reload (without Refresh) would still show for up to an hour.

title: Combining search + status + domain + asset-type filters narrows results to the strict intersection
preconditions: Framework has controls across at least 2 domains, mixed coverage statuses, and mixed asset attachments
steps: Set search text matching a subset of control titles
Set statusFilter to 'partial'
Set domainFilter to a specific domain code
Set assetFilter to 'evidence' (Has Evidence)
Read the '<N> of <Total> controls' counter and the visible accordion rows
expectedResult: Only controls satisfying all four predicates simultaneously (title/ID matches search AND coverageStatus==='partial' AND domain matches AND _evidenceCount>0) are shown; the counter matches the number of visible rows exactly, and domains with zero matching controls after filtering are hidden from the accordion entirely.

title: The Navbar header updates dynamically to the framework's real title once compliance-map data loads
steps: Navigate directly to /grc-framework/:id/compliance-map via a bookmarked URL (cold load)
Observe the page/nav header text before and after data finishes loading
expectedResult: Before data loads, the header shows a generic/placeholder title. Once loadData resolves, setPageHeader updates it to '<Framework Title> — Compliance Map' with the subtitle 'Control-by-control coverage tracker · evidence, policies, vendors and cloud checks', and the header reverts/clears when navigating away (clearPageHeader on unmount).
